rule: What a walker sees from the street, 2-3 English sentences. Only what is visible in the listed photos or stated in the listed text sources. Season-only things (snow, flowers, lanterns) are left out or marked. No photo and no text = not written.

items.text: A large walled palace at the foot of a rocky, cone-shaped mountain (Bugaksan). From outside you see a long pale stone wall with a gate tower in front, and behind it many halls with dark grey tiled roofs.
basis_text: Official Royal Palaces site: 'Mountain (also known as Bugaksan Mountain) at the backdrop, and a wide Yukjo Street unfolds before Gwanghwamun Gate'

items.text: A two-tiered wooden gate tower with grey tiled roofs and painted eaves, sitting on a long pale stone base pierced by three arched openings. A wide raised stone terrace with low stone railings stretches out in front of it, and stone walls run off to both sides.
Inside Gwanghwamun, across a wide sandy courtyard, stands a second gate with a two-tiered roof, joined on both sides by long single-storey corridors with red pillars.

The largest hall: two storeys of deep painted eaves under grey tiled roofs, set on a two-level stone platform with carved stone railings and central stairs. A wide courtyard paved with rough stone slabs lies in front, with mountains behind.
A very large open pavilion raised on rows of stone pillars, standing in a square pond. Its long grey tiled roof is reflected in the water, and small islands with pine trees sit beside it.
A small, slender two-storey pavilion with six sides and a pointed tiled roof, standing on a grassy island in a pond. The rocky peak of Bugaksan rises behind it.
A small square watchtower with a tiled pavilion roof on top of a tall block of cut stone. It stands alone at a road junction, with cars passing and modern glass towers behind it.

A long, low modern building with a traditional-style tiled roof edge, reached by a broad flight of stone steps. The name '국립고궁박물관 / National Palace Museum of Korea' is on a dark board above the glass entrance.
A tall five-tiered pagoda-shaped tower rises above a white stone building with wide twin stairways. It stands at the north-east side of the palace grounds, with a large open forecourt in front.
basis_text: OSM location: inside the Gyeongbokgung grounds

items.text: A wide paved square beside the main road, Sejong-daero, with planted beds, umbrellas and large statues. At its north end, across a road crossing, you look straight at Gwanghwamun Gate with mountains behind.
basis_text: Wikivoyage Seoul/Jongno 'Get in': 'walk along Sejong-daero, a busy road that passes Gwanghwamun Plaza. The plaza has statues and monuments honoring Sejong the Great and Admiral Yi Sun-sin'

items.text: A large golden-bronze statue of a seated king on a throne, one hand raised, holding an open book in the other. It sits on a stone plinth carved with '세종대왕' (King Sejong the Great) in Korean letters.

A dark bronze statue of an armoured admiral holding a long sword, standing on a tall stone pillar at the south end of the square. Looking north past it you can see the mountains and the palace gate in the distance.
A wide, flat-fronted modern building in pale grey with long horizontal bands, facing Sejong-daero, with a flagpole and lawn in front. The museum name is on the upper part of the facade.
A three-storey red-brick building with rows of large steel-framed windows and a white entrance canopy carrying the museum name in Korean and English. Low steps lead up from the street.
A gently sloping street with cafes and small shops lined up on top of a stone retaining wall, some with umbrellas on roof terraces. A row of trees and a low railing run along the pavement.

A three-storey pale yellow building in an old school style with a central arched doorway, behind a garden with pine trees. A round fountain basin with a white bowl-shaped centrepiece sits in front of it.

Steep, narrow paved lanes lined with hanok houses: grey curved tiled roofs, wooden gates and patterned stone walls. From the upper lanes you can look down over the roofs to downtown high-rises and a tower on a hill (N Seoul Tower).
basis_text: Bukchon Red Zone: tourist visits only 10:00-17:00 (Jongno-gu official page)

items.text: A narrow lane between old walls of stone and brick, with hanok roofs on the right and trees hanging over the walls; the lane slopes down and bends out of sight.
basis_text: Photo description: 'near Bukchon-ro 11-gil street'. Not confirmed to be exactly the 5th scenic spot.

items.text: According to Wikivoyage it is a converted apartment with a rooftop view, 'tucked away' and easy to miss; from the top you can see over Bukchon to the palace and the city. (No photo.)

A tall traditional gate with its own small tiled roof, at the top of a wide flight of stone steps. Long white-plastered walls with grey tiled tops run to both sides, with a garden of shrubs and rocks below.
A long, low pale building with rows of identical windows and a modern glass-walled wing, around a wide open lawn and courtyard.
basis_text: Official page: on the historic site of Andong Byeolgung; 50 m from Anguk Station Exit 1

items.text: Inside the walls: a single-storey hanok hall on a high stone platform, with dark wooden pillars, white paper-panel doors and a grey tiled roof. Hanging boards with writing are fixed to the pillars.
A large two-storey wooden gate with red pillars, painted eaves and a double tiled roof, set back from the road behind a low railing and a small open plaza. Its name board reads 敦化門.

A big temple hall with richly painted green, red and blue woodwork and a steep tiled roof, with a red gable carrying a gold three-circle emblem. A large old tree with pale bark stands in the courtyard in front, next to a white stone statue.
A long street lined with tall trees, low shop buildings and small signs, wide enough for walkers to use the middle. Benches and planters sit along the edges.
basis_text: Jogyesa official page: 'Insa-dong is designated as a vehicle-free zone on Saturday afternoons and Sundays'

items.text: A four-storey building built around an open courtyard, with a walkway that ramps up around the yard past rows of small shops with glass fronts.

The park entrance is a wide traditional gate with green-painted woodwork, red pillars and a tiled roof, with a sign board reading '삼일문'. Inside is a paved yard with an eight-sided pavilion under a tiled roof.
basis_text: Wongaksa Pagoda and Palgakjeong are inside (OSM)

items.text: A red-brick building with white stone trim, a tall central tower topped by a small dome and spire, and a round window near the top of the tower. An arched doorway is at the foot of the tower.

A maze of very narrow paved alleys between low hanok with tiled roofs, now mostly cafes and small shops with painted doors and small signs. From above it is a dense patch of grey roofs surrounded by taller buildings.

not_written.L27: Museum Kimchikan: no photo of the current building and no text describing its outside.
